questions.q: If A – B means that A is the brother of B, A + B means that A is the sister of B, A ÷ B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal uncle of R?

questions.q: Which of the following climate type is found under the cold climates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tundra.

Key Points

• Among all the biomes, the tundra is the coldest.

• In addition, the tundra experiences little precipitation, which resembles a desert.

• Arctic tundra can be found in the areas immediately below the ice caps, and it can be found in Siberia in Asia, North America, and Europe.

• The tundra biome encompasses most of Alaska and roughly half of Canada.

• Several places throughout the world also have tundra on the summits of very tall mountains.

• With mean annual temperatures below 0°C during six to ten months of the year, tundra winters are protracted, dark, and cold.

• Permafrost, or permanently frozen ground, results from the area's extremely low temperatures.

• The tundra biome is distinguished by this permafrost.

• Only a few inches of the top layer of soil thaws during the tundra summers, giving vegetation roots a growth surface.

Additional Information

• Humid subtropical:

• ​A climate zone characterised mid summers and cold to mild winters is known as a humid subtropical climate.

• Highland:

• Highland climate features include high insolation, low temperatures, low air pressure, wide diurnal temperature fluctuations, and relatively heavy precipitation at higher altitudes.

• Humid continental:

• It is characterized by four distinct seasons, significant seasonal temperature changes, and frigid (often extremely cold) winters.

questions.q: What do you call the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Secondary productivity.

Key Points

• Primary productivity is the pace at which producers - plants and other photosynthetic organisms - create new organic matter.

• The rate at which consumers are creating new organic matter is known as secondary productivity. Protists, fungi, bacteria, Deer, cows, goats, horses, etc. are a few examples.

• The entire dry biomass of all living things at a certain trophic level is referred to as a standing crop.

• It stands for biomass that is above ground. It could vary during the course of the year.

• There are two forms of primary productivity:

• Gross primary productivity, which measures the total rate of photosynthesis and the amount of organic matter consumed during respiration and is influenced by chlorophyll content.

• The difference between gross primary production and ecosystem organisms' respiration is known as net primary production.

Additional Information

• Tertiary productivity:​

• ​The quantity of fresh biomass (weight) that carnivores (animals that eat meat) create over a certain amount of time.

• Primary Productivity:

• ​The process by which organisms produce their own sustenance from inorganic sources is known as primary productivity. Terrestrial plants and microbiological life, such as algae, make up the majority of primary producers.

• Net Productivity:

• ​The total amount of food or biomass produced by primary producers minus energy losses, which is also the total amount of food stored by producers, is referred to as net primary productivity.

questions.q: What is the structure of the Indian judiciary?
questions.solution:
The correct option is Three-tier.

Key Points

• The Indian judiciary is organized into a three-tier system:

• Supreme Court:

• At the top is the Supreme Court of India, which is the highest judicial authority in the country.

• It has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction.

• The Supreme Court has the power to hear appeals from lower courts, issue writs, and interpret the Constitution.

• High Courts:

• Each state in India has a High Court.

• High Courts are the second-highest courts in the country and have jurisdiction over their respective states or union territories.

• They have the power of superintendence over the subordinate courts within their jurisdiction.

• Subordinate Courts:

Calculation:
